name: Paper.design
subcategory: browser-based vector and motion design tool
tagline: A browser design tool for vector art, shader-style effects and animation, aimed at designers who want motion and texture without leaving the canvas.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: This is a real-time graphics editor, which is the genre of software that eats teams of specialists for years. The hard parts are not features, they are the boring invariants: a scene graph that never corrupts, boolean ops on bezier paths, snapping and alignment that feel right, undo across every operation, text layout, and a GPU render loop that stays at 60fps while you drag. An agent can absolutely give you a canvas with layers and a shader background in one session, and it will feel great for about ten minutes, until you try to edit a path node or nudge a group and discover the editor has no opinion about either. The actual output, files other people can open and effects that export cleanly, is also not something a weekend build produces. Build the toy for fun, keep the tool for work.
coreLoopDIY: A local WebGL canvas where you stack a few shapes and a parameterized shader gradient, tweak the parameters live, and export a PNG or an animated frame sequence.
requirements: Node and a local dev server
Patience for shader math, or an agent willing to write GLSL for you
whatYouLose: Real vector editing: pen tool, node editing, boolean operations, stroke profiles
Export anyone else can use, SVG, Lottie, video, or a design file that opens elsewhere
Text: fonts, kerning, wrapping, variable axes, none of which you want to implement
Multiplayer canvas, comments, version history, shareable links
The hundred invisible interaction details, snapping, smart guides, marquee select, that make an editor feel like a tool instead of a demo
moatNotes: Graphics editors are a polish moat with no shortcut: the value is in a thousand small correct behaviors, and each one is cheap to describe and expensive to get right.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the alternative is doing motion and texture work by bouncing between a vector tool, a motion tool and a shader playground, exporting between each one, and redoing it all when a parameter changes. A single canvas where effects stay live and editable saves real hours per project, and the subscription is cheap against one billable afternoon. People also pay for exports that land in a client deliverable without a conversion dance, which is precisely the part a local build skips.
notes: You can clone the shader playground in a weekend and it will even look good in a screenshot. The moat is the editor underneath it: path editing, snapping, text, undo, and export that other software accepts.
prompt:
Build a local, single-user shader gradient playground in an empty folder. This is a toy graphics tool, not a design app, and not a clone of a commercial editor.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Vite + TypeScript, no framework
- Raw WebGL2, no three.js, no regl
- Zustand for state, Tailwind for the panel UI
- Everything runs with `npm run dev`, no accounts, no backend, no telemetry

What it does:
- Full-window canvas rendering a fullscreen fragment shader
- A right side panel of controls bound live to shader uniforms: 2 to 5 color stops, noise scale, noise octaves, warp amount, grain amount, animation speed, blur radius
- A preset dropdown with 6 hardcoded presets, each just a JSON blob of uniform values
- Animation driven by a uTime uniform in a requestAnimationFrame loop, with a pause button
- Overlay layer: user can add rectangles, ellipses and lines on top of the gradient, drag them, set fill color and opacity. Store them as plain objects in Zustand and draw them in a second pass. No grouping, no path editing, no text.
- Export PNG at 1x and 2x via canvas.toBlob
- Export the current uniform set as JSON, and import it back
- Undo/redo for uniform and shape changes, using a simple state snapshot stack capped at 50 entries
- Persist the current document to localStorage on change, restore on load

Explicitly out of scope, do not attempt:
- Pen tool, bezier node editing, boolean operations
- Text layers and font handling
- SVG, Lottie or video export
- Multiplayer, sharing links, cloud storage, auth

Write the GLSL inline as template strings in a shaders/ directory. Include a README with the keyboard shortcuts and one paragraph saying plainly what this cannot do. If any secret is ever needed, read it from .env, but nothing here should need one.
